preamble: Diphthongization of a nasal back vowel [õ]/[ɔ̃] into a back nasal diphthong [õw̃] or [ɔw̃] (mapped to the ou cell). Polish ą, a nasal monophthong in older Polish, is realized [ɔw̃] before non-palatal fricatives and word-finally (są 'they are', wąs 'moustache'). In Portuguese the word-final nasal vowel of bom 'good' and som 'sound' is commonly realized [õw̃], although its diphthongal status is disputed and it may be monophthongized to [õ].

examples.note: Before non-palatal fricatives (f, w, s, z, sz, ż, rz, ch) and word-finally ą is an oral vowel plus a nasalized glide [w̃]; before stops it splits into vowel + nasal consonant instead.
Word-final -om is listed as [õw̃] ~ [õ]; the diphthongal analysis is controversial.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Portuguese phonology, section Nasal diphthongs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_phonology
context: Polish: before non-palatal fricatives and word-finally; Portuguese: word-final -om
